title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 6 Triangles (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number. No calculator.

S1.name: Similar figures
S1.tip: Similar = same shape. Polygons need BOTH equal angles AND sides in one ratio (a square and a rhombus are not similar). Congruent figures are always similar.

S2.name: BPT: statement and proof
S2.tip: BPT: DE ∥ BC → AD/DB = AE/EC. Proof: join BE, CD; heights EN and DM; ar(BDE) = ar(DEC) (same base DE, same parallels).

S3.name: BPT with numbers (DE ∥ BC)
S3.tip: Use AD/DB = AE/EC or AD/AB = AE/AC. For DE itself use △ADE ~ △ABC: DE/BC = AD/AB, not AD/DB.

S4.name: Converse of BPT
S4.tip: Converse: equal ratios on two sides → the line is parallel to the third side. Compute both ratios and compare.
S4.ncert: NCERT Theorem 6.2, Example 3; Exercise 6.2 Q2, Q8

S5.name: BPT in trapeziums and figures
S5.tip: In a trapezium, join a diagonal to get two triangles, apply BPT in each, then equate. Diagonals meeting at O: AO/BO = CO/DO.
S5.ncert: NCERT Example 2; Exercise 6.2 Q3, Q4, Q9, Q10

S6.name: Similarity criteria and correspondence
S6.tip: AA, SSS, SAS. The order of letters fixes the pairs: △ABC ~ △EDF means A ↔ E, B ↔ D, C ↔ F.

S7.name: Sides and perimeters of similar triangles
S7.tip: Corresponding sides share one ratio, and so do the perimeters. Pair the sides by the correspondence before writing the ratio.

S8.name: Similarity proofs and medians
S8.tip: Pick the criterion from the data (parallel lines → AA; a product → SAS). ∠ADC = ∠BAC → CA² = CB·CD. Medians are in the ratio of the sides.

S9.name: Shadows and heights
S9.tip: Same time → parallel sun rays → height/shadow is the same. Lamp-post: lamp/person = (distance + shadow)/shadow. Convert cm to m first.

questions.question: Which pair of figures is always similar?
questions.explanation: All squares have equal angles (90°) and sides in one ratio.

questions.question: Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Congruent figures have the same shape and size, so they are similar; the converse fails.
options: Two rhombuses with equal sides are always similar
Two triangles with equal areas are similar

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The sides are in ratio 1 : 1 but the angles (90° vs 60°) differ, so A is false; R is the correct rule.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: both conditions are needed.
questions.assertion: A square of side 4 cm and a rhombus of side 4 cm with an angle of 60° are similar.
questions.reason: Two polygons with the same number of sides are similar only if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Two quadrilaterals have all corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 3, but their angles are not equal. The quadrilaterals are:
questions.explanation: For polygons, proportional sides alone are not enough; angles must also be equal.
options: Similar only if they are squares

questions.question: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC with D on AB and E on AC. By the Basic Proportionality Theorem:
questions.explanation: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides in the same ratio.

questions.question: In the proof of BPT, why is ar(△BDE) = ar(△DEC)?
questions.explanation: Same base, same parallels → equal areas. This is the key step.
options: They are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC

questions.question: In the proof of BPT, ar(△ADE)/ar(△BDE) = AD/DB because:
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × base × height; with the same height EN the area ratio is the base ratio AD/DB.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: the construction EN ⊥ AB.
options: Both triangles have the same base DE
Both triangles have the same height EN from E to AB

questions.question: The Basic Proportionality Theorem is also known as:
questions.explanation: NCERT names BPT the Thales theorem.

questions.question: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 4 cm. Find EC (in cm).
questions.explanation: AD/DB = AE/EC → 2/3 = 4/EC → EC = 6.

questions.question: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 6 cm, AB = 15 cm and AC = 20 cm. Find AE (in cm).
questions.explanation: AD/AB = AE/AC → 6/15 = AE/20 → AE = 8.

questions.question: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC. AD = 4 cm, DB = 8 cm and BC = 18 cm. Find DE (in cm).
questions.explanation: △ADE ~ △ABC, so DE/BC = AD/AB = 4/12 → DE = 6.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: DE uses AD/AB, not AD/DB.

questions.question: In △ABC, DE ∥ BC. AD = x, DB = x − 2, AE = x + 2 and EC = x − 1. The value of x is:
In △PQR, ST ∥ QR with S on PQ and T on PR. PS = 3 cm, SQ = 6 cm and PR = 12 cm. Find TR (in cm).
questions.explanation: PS/PQ = PT/PR → 3/9 = PT/12 → PT = 4, TR = 8.

questions.question: E and F are points on PQ and PR of △PQR. Which data shows EF ∥ QR?
questions.explanation: 4/4.5 = 8/9 and 8/9: equal ratios → parallel (converse of BPT).

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: 3/6 = 4/8 = 1/2, so A is true, and R (the converse of BPT) is exactly why.
questions.assertion: In △PQR, PE = 3 cm, EQ = 6 cm, PF = 4 cm and FR = 8 cm, so EF ∥ QR.
questions.reason: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: In △PQR, PS/SQ = PT/TR (S on PQ, T on PR) and ∠PST = ∠PRQ. Then △PQR is:
questions.explanation: ST ∥ QR → ∠PST = ∠PQR; with ∠PST = ∠PRQ, ∠PQR = ∠PRQ → PQ = PR (NCERT Example 3).

questions.question: D and E are the mid-points of AB and AC of △ABC. Using the converse of BPT, DE is:
questions.explanation: AD/DB = 1 = AE/EC → DE ∥ BC (NCERT Exercise 6.2 Q8).

questions.question: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC, and its diagonals meet at O. Which is true?
questions.explanation: △AOB ~ △COD (alternate angles) → AO/CO = BO/DO → AO/BO = CO/DO.

questions.question: ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. E on AD and F on BC with EF ∥ AB. AE = 3 cm, ED = 6 cm and BF = 4 cm. Find FC (in cm).
questions.explanation: Join AC: AE/ED = BF/FC → 3/6 = 4/FC → FC = 8.

questions.question: In a trapezium PQRS with PQ ∥ SR, XY ∥ PQ (X on PS, Y on QR). To prove PX/XS = QY/YR, the first step is to:
questions.explanation: The diagonal splits the trapezium into two triangles where BPT applies.
options: Join the diagonal PR (meeting XY at M)
Extend PS and QR to meet
Join the mid-points of PQ and SR

questions.question: In △ABC, D is on AB, E is on BC and F is on BE. If DE ∥ AC and DF ∥ AE, then:
questions.explanation: In △BAC, DE ∥ AC → BD/DA = BE/EC; in △BAE, DF ∥ AE → BD/DA = BF/FE; so BF/FE = BE/EC (NCERT Exercise 6.2 Q4).

questions.question: If △ABC ~ △PQR, which is true?
questions.explanation: Order of letters fixes the pairs: A ↔ P, B ↔ Q, C ↔ R.

questions.question: If △ABC ~ △EDF, which statement is NOT true?
questions.explanation: A ↔ E, B ↔ D, C ↔ F, so ∠A = ∠E, not ∠D (2026 board type).

questions.question: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠B = ∠E, ∠F = ∠C and AB = 3 DE. The triangles are:
questions.explanation: Two angles equal → AA similar; AB ≠ DE so not congruent (2025 board type).

questions.question: Sides of two triangles are 3, 4, 5 cm and 6, 8, 10 cm. They are similar by:
questions.explanation: 3/6 = 4/8 = 5/10 = 1/2: all three side ratios equal → SSS.

questions.question: In △ABC and △PQR, AB/PQ = AC/PR and ∠A = ∠P. Then:
questions.explanation: One equal angle with the including sides in ratio → SAS similarity.

questions.question: △ABC ~ △DEF and AB/DE = 3/5. If the perimeter of △DEF is 40 cm, find the perimeter of △ABC (in cm).
questions.explanation: Perimeters are in the ratio of the sides: 40 × 3/5 = 24.

questions.question: The perimeters of two similar triangles are 30 cm and 45 cm. A side of the first is 12 cm. Find the corresponding side of the second (in cm).
△ABC ~ △QPR. AC = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and QR = 4 cm. Find PR (in cm).
questions.explanation: A ↔ Q, B ↔ P, C ↔ R: AC ↔ QR, BC ↔ PR → 8/4 = 6/PR → PR = 3.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: pair the sides by correspondence.

questions.question: △ABC ~ △DEF with AB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm, EF = 9 cm and FD = 12 cm. Find the perimeter of △ABC (in cm).
questions.explanation: Ratio 4/6 = 2/3; perimeter of △DEF = 27 → 27 × 2/3 = 18.

questions.question: In the figure, PQ ∥ RS and PS, QR meet at O. Then:
questions.explanation: Alternate angles ∠P = ∠S, ∠Q = ∠R and vertically opposite angles at O → △POQ ~ △SOR (NCERT Example 4).

questions.question: D is a point on BC of △ABC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. If CA = 6 cm and CD = 4 cm, find CB (in cm).
questions.explanation: △ADC ~ △BAC → CA/CD = CB/CA → CA² = CB·CD → 36 = 4 CB → CB = 9.

questions.question: In △PQR, S is a point on PR such that ∠PQR = ∠QSP. PQ = 8 cm and PS = 4 cm. Find PR (in cm).
questions.explanation: △PQR ~ △PSQ (∠P common, ∠PQR = ∠PSQ) → PQ/PS = PR/PQ → 8/4 = PR/8 → PR = 16.

questions.question: In the figure, OA · OB = OC · OD, with AB and CD meeting at O. Which criterion proves △AOD ~ △COB?
questions.explanation: OA/OD = OC/OB with the vertically opposite angle at O between them → SAS (NCERT Example 6).

questions.question: △ABC ~ △PQR with AB = 10 cm and PQ = 15 cm. The median from C of △ABC is 8 cm. Find the median from R of △PQR (in cm).
questions.explanation: Medians are in the ratio of the sides: 8 × 15/10 = 12 (NCERT Example 8).

questions.question: Sides AB, BC and median AD of △ABC are proportional to sides PQ, QR and median PM of △PQR. The proof that △ABC ~ △PQR first shows:
questions.explanation: BD = BC/2 and QM = QR/2 share the ratio, so △ABD ~ △PQM (SSS) → ∠B = ∠Q → SAS for the big triangles.

questions.question: A 4 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. At the same time a tower casts a 24 m shadow. Find the height of the tower (in m).
A 12 m tower casts a 9 m shadow. At the same time a pole casts a 6 m shadow. Find the height of the pole (in m).
A boy 1.5 m tall stands 6 m from a lamp-post 4.5 m high. The length of his shadow is:
A girl 80 cm tall walks away from a lamp 4 m high at 1 m/s. Find the length of her shadow (in cm) after 4 seconds.
questions.explanation: She is 4 m away. 4/0.8 = (4 + x)/x → 5x = 4 + x → x = 1 m = 100 cm.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: change cm to m first.
